Tooling review of the GLM exam-bank lane. I ran everything against copies in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-pabloillescas-Documents-GitHub-pyarcana/7ce613dd-3e23-4ed3-b165-9bffbd388440/scratchpad/glm-bank/tooling-review/ (base/, replay/, fa/, fr/, fau/, lc/). The owner's tree was only read.

Its §6 says: "every active section's slug must be present in QUESTION_BANK with ≥8 concepts and exactly 3 variants per concept, and the count of covered sections is a floor that can never worsen (47 today...)".

Verdict: not approvable as is. Provenance is good: the codex results are on disk in .fixer, and the working seed matches them exactly. The tooling itself is weak.
- apply_bank_repairs.py can never repair slot 23 (its own balance gate catches it). It silently reverts a later repair when an earlier set is rerun. It lets 3- or 5-option questions and raw CR characters through, and a CR produces invalid TypeScript.
- rebalance_exam_bank_positions.py only sees the 5 double-quoted bank keys. One valid TS formatting variant makes --write move 20 of 24 answers off the cycle while it still reports uniform_ok=true. It has no write gates.
- The new audit checks never check correctIndex positions. Its cosmetic-rewording check catches only exact duplicates. "Exactly 3 variants" is report-only. Deleting the floor file lets coverage regress with exit 0.
- Complexity over the ceiling of 15: apply main is 54, bracket_balance 28, rebalance main 21, bank_balance_issues 18, and audit main rose from 16 to 27.

D15's premise that the base covered "47 of 52" is false at HEAD 29f0af20. The new ratchet code itself reports 52/52 on the HEAD seed. Whether production DBs really served 404s is UNDETERMINED.

The LONGEST_IS_CORRECT_OWED=1125 ratchet is not in HEAD. It lives only in .claude/worktrees/test-hardening (commit 5f36c888, branch claude/ci-done-gates). Its measure falls to 1079 on the working seed, so its equality test would fail until the constant is lowered. Its docstring rule "never trim the key" conflicts with the GLM S08bandfix prompt, which says "Trim the correct option to the band".

Research: Haladyna, Downing and Rodriguez (2002) support D15 §4. Their guidelines say to vary the key position and keep option lengths about equal (https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ660246, https://cmapspublic3.ihmc.us/rid=1P2XTLCSS-11K09T9-BD5/Haladyna_2002_-Appl_Meas_Educ.pdf). The TypeScript compiler API (ts.createSourceFile with parseDiagnostics) is the standard syntactic check (https://learning-notes.mistermicheels.com/javascript/typescript/compiler-api/). The repo already uses it in scripts/rebalance_selfcheck_positions.mjs, and the GLM scripts use regex instead.

result.summary:
Item-quality review of the glm-5.3/codex exam-bank work, which is uncommitted in the owner's tree (base 29f0af20). Everything ran on scratch copies under /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-pabloillescas-Documents-GitHub-pyarcana/7ce613dd-3e23-4ed3-b165-9bffbd388440/scratchpad/glm-bank/item-quality/. The owner's tree was only read.

Scope of the change: I evaluated the QUESTION_BANK literal for HEAD and for the working tree (node, extract.mjs). Both have 52 keys and 1248 questions; the other 2 'question:' hits fall outside the bank. Only 118 questions changed, all of them in 5 sections: functions-contracts (S05) 24, files-ingestion (S08) 23, exceptions-logging (S09) 24, modules-packaging-cli (S10) 23, oop-domain (S11) 24. No other section was touched. Of the 118, 6 changed position only and 112 were rewritten. Nothing is left to spread across other sections, so I judged all 118 against their HEAD versions.

Research: I used the NBME Item-Writing Guide, 6th edition, current PDF. Its preface is dated August 2020, its copyright line reads '1996 ... 2020, 2024', and the PDF was modified 2024-11-04. Its 'Flaws that cue the testwise examinee' (pp. 21-24) and the summary table (p. 25) cover grammatical cues, collectively exhaustive options, absolute terms, 'Correct Option Stands Out', word repetition (clang clues), convergence and 'None of the above'. On length, p. 23 says the flaw arises because writers 'construct long correct answers that include additional instructional material'. The fix on p. 25 is 'Revise options to equal length. Remove language used for teaching points and rationales.' The same table lists 'Long, complex options -> Put common text in stem; parallel construction; shorten options'. I also used Haladyna, Downing and Rodriguez (2002), whose guideline is to keep options about equal in length. The course rules come from audit/fixer/writing_rules.md.

Verdicts for the 118 items:
- better: 92 (78%)
- same: 20 (17%)
- worse: 6 (5%)
- wrong key: 0

result.summary:
Docs-check lane. I read PR #81's files with git show and wrote nothing in the owner's tree. Every doc I fetched went to scratchpad/glm-bank/docs-check/ (GitHub docs raw-article API, the GitHub REST OpenAPI description, actions/* READMEs and sources, and the scipy 1.13.1 HTML docs plus the v1.13.1 source).

(1) deploy.yml on origin/claude/renumber-phase0-sentinel. Every claim it relies on is CONFIRMED by the current GitHub docs:
- Under workflow_run, GITHUB_SHA is "Last commit on default branch".
- head_sha, head_branch, event and conclusion exist, and 'success' and 'push' are valid values.
- The branches filter applies to the branch the triggering workflow ran on.
- The workflow file must exist on the default branch.
- Pages deploys need pages: write and id-token: write. No doc restricts the triggering event.

Two NUANCED points:
- The security caveat applies only weakly. This workflow checks out and builds head_sha, which is safe only because of the event=='push' && head_branch=='main' guard.
- The workflow-level `concurrency: cancel-in-progress: true` runs before the job-level `if`. So a deploy run that later skips can still cancel a real deploy that is in progress. GitHub's own Pages starter uses cancel-in-progress: false.

Two version notes, both also true on main: upload-pages-artifact@v3 and deploy-pages@v4 are not the latest (v5.0.0 and v5.0.1), and both declare node20. GitHub forced node20 actions onto Node 24 from 16 June 2026 and removed Node 20 on 23 September 2026.

(2) scipy is pinned at requirements-content.txt:20 (scipy==1.13.1). Every assumed API is CONFIRMED in the 1.13.1 docs:
- BinomTestResult.proportion_ci accepts method='wilson'. The default is 'exact'.
- chi2_contingency has correction=True.
- ttest_ind has equal_var=True; False gives Welch's test.
- f_oneway(*samples, ...) and chisquare(f_obs, f_exp=None, ddof=0, axis=0) exist.
- t.ppf(q, df) and norm.ppf(q) exist.

I also ran each call in .venv-content (Python 3.12.12, scipy 1.13.1) with -B and PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1, from the scratchpad. All of them work. I could not find the statistics design document in the repo or the session scratchpad. The signatures it 'assumed' are therefore UNDETERMINED. I can only report the signatures that exist.

(3) The forty-zeros `before` on a push that creates a branch is NUANCED. GitHub's push webhook schema (docs and OpenAPI) describes `before` only as "The SHA of the most recent commit on ref before the push" and never mentions zeros. A WebFetch summary claimed it did; the raw text shows it does not. The zeros are documented officially only for the receive side, in the GHES pre-receive hook doc and in git's githooks(5). Community reports confirm github.event.before is forty zeros in Actions. The sentinel test /^0+$/ is robust to the length. Its fallback (merge-base with origin/main) works because checkout with fetch-depth: 0 fetches all branches.

D15 is quoted from audit/fixer/decisions.md:389-431.

findings.claim: CONFIRMED: under workflow_run, github.sha / GITHUB_SHA is the default branch's last commit, not the commit of the triggering run. The deploy.yml comment (lines 7-9) and its use of workflow_run.head_sha are correct.
findings.evidence: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows#workflow_run: table row for workflow_run reads `GITHUB_SHA` = 'Last commit on default branch', `GITHUB_REF` = 'Default branch' (raw article line 1239). Nuance: this is the tip when the run is created, not when a step executes. deploy.yml re-checks the tip with `git fetch origin main` (lines 45-52), which closes that gap. The actions/deploy-pages@v4 source labels the deployment with process.env.GITHUB_SHA (src/internal/context.js:8, `buildVersion: process.env.GITHUB_SHA`). That label can differ from head_sha only if main went backwards, so it is harmless.

findings.claim: CONFIRMED: github.event.workflow_run has head_sha, head_branch, event and conclusion, and 'success' and 'push' are documented values.
findings.evidence: GitHub REST OpenAPI description (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/github/rest-api-description/main/descriptions/api.github.com/api.github.com.json), schema webhook-workflow-run-completed.workflow_run: head_branch {string, nullable}, head_sha {string}, event {string} (the workflow-run schema shows example 'push'), conclusion enum [action_required, cancelled, failure, neutral, skipped, stale, success, timed_out, startup_failure]. The events doc gives the `github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success'` pattern verbatim (raw article line 1274).

findings.claim: CONFIRMED with a nuance: `branches: [main]` filters on the branch the triggering workflow ran on, which is workflow_run.head_branch. For a fork PR, head_branch is the fork's branch name, so a fork PR from a branch named 'main' passes the filter. deploy.yml's job-level `event == 'push'` guard covers this case.
findings.evidence: events-that-trigger-workflows raw line 1297: 'You can use the `branches` or `branches-ignore` filter to specify what branches the triggering workflow must run on in order to trigger your workflow.' The fork-PR nuance is an inference from head_branch being 'the ref that triggered' the run. The docs do not state it explicitly.

findings.claim: CONFIRMED: the workflow file must exist on the default branch. Until PR #81 merges, the trigger is inert, and main's current push/workflow_dispatch deploy.yml keeps deploying in parallel with Tests. The PR cannot be exercised end-to-end in CI before the merge.
findings.evidence: events-that-trigger-workflows, workflow_run note (raw line 1244): 'This event will only trigger a workflow run if the workflow file exists on the default branch.' `git show origin/main:.github/workflows/deploy.yml` still has `push:` (line 4) and `workflow_dispatch:` (line 6).

findings.claim: NUANCED: the workflow-level `concurrency: {group: pages, cancel-in-progress: true}` is evaluated when the run is queued, before the job `if`. Any deploy run that later skips can therefore cancel a real deploy that is in progress. Example: Tests completes for a fork PR whose head branch is 'main' (Tests runs on pull_request into main). GitHub's own Pages starter workflow sets cancel-in-progress: false and explains why. main's deploy.yml already had cancel-in-progress: true, so PR #81 does not introduce this.
findings.evidence: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-when-workflows-run/control-workflow-concurrency (raw line 13): 'To also cancel any currently running job or workflow in the same concurrency group, specify `cancel-in-progress: true`.' https://raw.githubusercontent.com/actions/starter-workflows/main/pages/static.yml: '# However, do NOT cancel in-progress runs as we want to allow these production deployments to complete.' followed by `cancel-in-progress: false`. deploy.yml lines 21-23.

findings.claim: CONFIRMED: the permissions and Pages actions work from a workflow_run trigger. deploy-pages requires only pages: write and id-token: write on the job and the github-pages environment, with no restriction on the triggering event. A workflow_run run also gets write tokens even when the triggering workflow did not. Environment protection rules see GITHUB_REF = the default branch (main), so a 'main only' deployment-branch policy passes.
findings.evidence: https://github.com/actions/deploy-pages/blob/v4/README.md lines 76-80: 'The job that executes the deployment must at minimum have the following permissions: pages: write, id-token: write'; 'The deployment should target the github-pages environment'. Events doc raw line 1247: 'The workflow started by the `workflow_run` event is able to access secrets and write tokens, even if the previous workflow was not.' deploy.yml lines 16-19 and 87-88 match. The artifact is uploaded and deployed within the same run, so there is no cross-workflow artifact trust issue.

findings.claim: NUANCED: GitHub's documented workflow_run security caveat applies weakly here. The run is privileged (pages: write, id-token: write) and runs `bun install` and a build on the checked-out head_sha. That is safe only because the job condition limits it to push events on main, whose code only maintainers can push. As defense in depth, a `github.event.workflow_run.head_repository.full_name == github.repository` check is not present.
findings.evidence: Events doc raw line 1250: 'Running untrusted code on the `workflow_run` trigger may lead to security vulnerabilities. These vulnerabilities include cache poisoning and granting unintended access to write privileges or secrets.' https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/secure-use#mitigating-the-risks-of-untrusted-code-checkout (raw line 100): 'Workflows that use these triggers must not explicitly check out untrusted code, including from pull request forks...' deploy.yml lines 27-30 and 35-38.
